products.name: TESK
products.tagline: GA4GH TES for any Kubernetes cluster
products.blurb: A task execution service that runs containerized tasks as Kubernetes jobs and needs no database or other services of its own.
products.description: TESK lets workflow engines and WES implementations run containerized tasks on a Kubernetes cluster. It implements the GA4GH TES API and runs each task as Kubernetes jobs in one namespace, staging its inputs and outputs in a temporary volume. Inputs and outputs can come from and go to HTTP(S), FTP, S3 or a shared file system, depending on the storage that a deployment configures. TESK needs no database of its own and is deployed with a Helm chart.
audience: Workflow engines and WES implementations that submit tasks through TES
Operators who offer TES on Kubernetes, without a database to run
features: Implements the GA4GH TES API
Runs each task as Kubernetes jobs in one namespace
Stages data via HTTP(S), FTP, S3 or a shared file system
Needs no database or other services of its own
howItWorks: The API validates each task it receives and creates a taskmaster job for it.
For a task with inputs, outputs or volumes, the taskmaster creates a temporary volume (PVC) as its scratch space.
The filer downloads the inputs into the volume, from HTTP(S), FTP, S3 or a shared file system.
The executors run one after the other, each as a job with the volume mounted.
The filer uploads the outputs; then the volume is deleted and the task ends.
requirements: A Kubernetes cluster, version 1.23 or later; TESK needs access to one namespace only
A default storage class (ReadWriteOnce is enough) for the temporary volume of each task with inputs or outputs
For inputs and outputs over anything but HTTP(S): an FTP account, a shared file system (a ReadWriteMany volume) or S3

products.name: proTES
products.tagline: GA4GH TES gateway for federated compute
products.blurb: A gateway that gives clients one GA4GH TES endpoint for a network of TES instances, and forwards each task to an instance that its plugins choose.
products.description: proTES lets operators offer one TES endpoint for independently operated TES instances. It implements the GA4GH TES API, so clients send tasks to it as to any TES instance; each task passes a pipeline of plugins, is forwarded and is tracked. By default, tasks go to a random instance; plugins can route them closest to their input data, or add access control and validation. Run it with Docker Compose, or deploy it to Kubernetes with its Helm chart.
audience: Operators who federate several TES instances behind one endpoint
Developers who write plugins for gateways
features: Implements the GA4GH TES API
Forwards each task to a TES instance that its plugin pipeline chooses
Routes tasks to the instance closest to their data, as an opt-in plugin
Requires access tokens and keeps each task with the user who created it
quickStart: Open the Swagger UI at http://localhost:8080/ga4gh/tes/v1/ui
List your TES instances under custom.tes.backends in config.dev.yaml, and set your identity provider there

products.name: Cloud Registry
products.tagline: GA4GH Service Registry for your network
products.blurb: A registry of web services that lets clients find the GA4GH and other services of a project, network or infrastructure, with their types, versions and operators.
products.description: Cloud Registry gives a project, network or infrastructure one place to list its web services, so that clients can find them. It implements the GA4GH Service Registry API, with entries in its ExternalService schema. Anyone can read the entries unless login is required; users who log in through a trusted OpenID Connect provider register and manage their services, and admins verify them and curate service types. Run it with Docker Compose, or deploy it to Kubernetes with its Helm chart.
audience: Operators who need one list of the services in their network
Service providers and client developers who register or find services
features: Implements the GA4GH Service Registry API
Lets logged-in users register and manage the services they own
Lets admins verify services and curate service types
Trusts several OpenID Connect providers at the same time

products.name: FOCA
products.tagline: Archetype for OpenAPI web services in Python
products.blurb: A Python archetype that builds a web service from OpenAPI specifications and one configuration file, so that developers write only the controllers and logic of their app.
products.description: FOCA lets Python developers build OpenAPI-based web services, such as GA4GH API implementations, without writing the common parts themselves. It builds a Connexion app on Flask from the specifications and a validated configuration, and adds token validation, access control with Casbin, MongoDB, background tasks and errors as problem details. Its plugin engine lets gateway apps check, change and route requests in pipelines that operators set. Signed Docker base images and a Helm library chart deploy FOCA apps.
audience: Developers who build GA4GH or other OpenAPI-based services in Python
Operators who deploy and configure FOCA-based services
features: Builds a web service from OpenAPI specifications and a configuration file
Validates access tokens and enforces access control with Casbin policies
Runs plugin pipelines that check, change and route requests in gateways
Ships signed Docker base images and a Helm library chart

products.name: Cloud Components
products.tagline: Web components for GA4GH API front ends
products.blurb: A library of web components that lets developers add views and forms for GA4GH and ELIXIR On-Cloud API services to any web front end, in any framework or in plain HTML.
products.description: Cloud Components gives front-end developers ready-made components for listing, viewing and managing the resources of ELIXIR On-Cloud and GA4GH API services. Its npm packages work with the GA4GH Service Registry, TRS, WES and DRS APIs, and with ELIXIR On-Cloud's Cloud Registry, TRS-Filer and DRS-Filer. Built with Lit and TypeScript, the components work in any framework, come with React wrappers and connect to your endpoints through providers. A shared design package adapts them to your brand.
audience: Front-end developers who build portals for GA4GH and ELIXIR On-Cloud services
Service developers who need a web interface for their API
features: Works with the GA4GH Service Registry, TRS, WES and DRS APIs and ELIXIR On-Cloud Services
Runs in any web framework or plain HTML, with React wrappers
Connects to your API endpoints through replaceable providers
Adapts to your brand through a shared design package

products.name: Poiesis
products.blurb: A task execution service that runs each containerized task as one Kubernetes pod and keeps the tasks, their states and their logs in PostgreSQL.
products.description: Poiesis lets workflow engines and users run containerized tasks on a Kubernetes cluster. It implements version 1.1 of the GA4GH TES API; each task runs as one pod that stages its inputs and outputs, and a controller records its state and logs in PostgreSQL. Users log in through an OpenID Connect provider and see only their own tasks; task pods run with restricted security settings, in a namespace of their own. Poiesis is deployed with a Helm chart.
audience: Workflow engines and users who submit tasks through TES
Operators who offer TES on Kubernetes, with login and a task history
features: Implements version 1.1 of the GA4GH TES API
Runs each task as one pod, in a namespace separate from the service
Records tasks, their states and their logs in PostgreSQL
Shows users only their own tasks, after OpenID Connect login

products.name: Pubgrade
products.blurb: A publish-subscribe service that notifies deployments of new images of the software they run, so that each deployment can update itself.
products.description: Pubgrade lets software developers tell every deployment of their software about a new image at once. A repository's CI publishes the image to Pubgrade, which notifies all deployments that subscribed to that branch or tag, and records the result for each. Each deployment decides what to do with a notification; Pubgrade-Sidecar, running next to a Kubernetes Deployment, updates its image. Deploy Pubgrade to Kubernetes or OpenShift with its Helm chart.
audience: Developers who publish new images of their software
Operators who want their deployments to update themselves
features: Receives new images from a repository's CI
Notifies all deployments that subscribed to a branch or tag
Records the result of each notification per subscriber
Updates Kubernetes Deployments through Pubgrade-Sidecar

products.name: GA4GH SDK
products.tagline: Rust SDK and CLI for GA4GH APIs
products.blurb: A software development kit and command-line client that let developers and users work with GA4GH TES, WES, DRS, TRS and Service Registry services from one library.
products.description: The GA4GH SDK lets developers build clients for GA4GH API services, and lets users call those services from the command line or from scripts. It works with the GA4GH TES, WES, DRS, TRS and Service Registry APIs, reads what each service supports from its service info, and handles authentication. The Rust library comes with Python bindings and a CLI; SDKs for services with API extensions can build on it without forking it.
audience: Developers who build clients for GA4GH services in Rust or Python
Users who script tasks and workflow runs from the command line
features: Works with the GA4GH TES, WES, DRS, TRS and Service Registry APIs
Offers the same clients as a Rust library, Python bindings and a CLI
Reads what each service supports from its service info
Lets other SDKs add endpoints and commands without forking it

products.name: Conquest
products.tagline: GA4GH WES for Nextflow, WDL and Snakemake
products.blurb: A workflow execution service that runs Nextflow, WDL and Snakemake workflows on Kubernetes, with their inputs and outputs in S3-compatible object storage.
products.description: Conquest lets researchers and platforms run Nextflow, WDL and Snakemake workflows on a Kubernetes cluster through one API. It implements the GA4GH WES API for runs and the GA4GH TES API for their tasks; each task runs as a Kubernetes job that stages its data from and to S3-compatible storage. Routing rules can send selected tasks to other TES services. Conquest is a single Go binary with PostgreSQL as its database, deployed with a Helm chart.
audience: Researchers who run Nextflow, WDL or Snakemake workflows
Operators who offer workflow execution on Kubernetes
features: Implements the GA4GH WES and TES APIs
Runs Nextflow, WDL and Snakemake, with the engine version chosen per run
Sets CPU, memory and disk per task, within platform limits
Sends selected tasks to other TES services, by routing rules

products.name: Funnel
products.tagline: GA4GH TES for HPC and cloud batch
products.blurb: A task execution service that runs containerized tasks on HPC schedulers, Kubernetes and cloud batch services, with their inputs and outputs in local or cloud storage.
products.description: Funnel lets workflow engines and users run containerized tasks on the compute systems they already have. It implements the GA4GH TES API: for each task, it finds a worker, downloads the inputs, runs the containers, uploads the outputs and records the logs. Compute backends include Slurm, HTCondor, Grid Engine, PBS/Torque, Kubernetes, AWS Batch and Google Cloud Batch; storage backends include S3, Google Cloud Storage, Swift, HTTP, FTP and local files. Funnel comes with a web dashboard.
audience: Workflow engines and users who submit tasks through TES
Operators who offer TES on HPC clusters or cloud accounts
features: Implements the GA4GH TES API
Runs tasks on Slurm, HTCondor, PBS/Torque, Grid Engine, Kubernetes and cloud batch
Stages data in S3, Google Cloud Storage, Swift, HTTP, FTP or local files
Shows tasks in a web dashboard

products.name: Krini
products.tagline: Web portal for GA4GH compute services
products.blurb: A web portal that lets researchers find compute services in a Cloud Registry, run tasks and workflows on them and follow their runs, without writing code.
products.description: Krini gives researchers one web interface for running analyses on the compute services of a network. It finds GA4GH TES and WES services in a Cloud Registry and lets logged-in users create tasks, submit workflow runs, follow their state and cancel them. Users log in through an OpenID Connect provider that the operator configures, and Krini passes their access token to the services. Operators deploy it with its image or Helm chart for their own registry, login provider and services.
audience: Researchers who run tasks and workflows without writing code
Operators who offer a portal to the services of their network
features: Works with the GA4GH TES, WES and Service Registry APIs
Lists the TES and WES services of a Cloud Registry
Creates and cancels tasks, submits workflow runs and follows both
Logs users in through a configurable OpenID Connect provider

products.name: TRS-Filer
products.tagline: GA4GH TRS for your tools and workflows
products.blurb: A registry of tools and workflows that lets workflow engines and execution services find them, with their versions and descriptors, and fetch their files.
products.description: TRS-Filer gives a project, network or infrastructure a registry of tools and workflows. It implements the GA4GH TRS API, so that workflow engines and execution services can find tools, their versions and classes, and fetch descriptors, test files and container image definitions, also as a ZIP archive. Additional endpoints register, update and delete entries, so it can host your own tools or index tools published elsewhere. Run it with Docker Compose, or deploy it to Kubernetes with its Helm chart.
audience: Workflow and tool authors who publish their tools
Developers of workflow engines and execution services that fetch tools
features: Implements the GA4GH TRS API
Serves descriptors, test files and container image definitions, also as ZIP
Registers, updates and deletes tools, versions and tool classes
Indexes tools that are published elsewhere
